patch.value: Native Bun path.matchesGlob rejects negative extglob duplication scopes

Bun 1.3.5 implements node:path.matchesGlob with different negative-extglob behavior from Node. The new dependency-free duplication matcher passes all six pinned filesystem contracts on Node, while a direct bun test run fails the negative-extglob assertion. Documented consumer duplication launchers use Node; native Bun packed acceptance passes for default globs. Track native Bun custom-pattern parity separately.

Reproduce the matcher difference using real filesystem fixtures and both runtimes.; Preserve dependency-free source discovery and unchanged 100% coverage thresholds while establishing native Bun negative-extglob parity or an explicit unsupported-pattern diagnostic.; Retain Node filesystem contracts and packed npm/native Bun default-glob clean and duplicate controls.

Compare matchesGlob("xsrc/xa.ts", "xsrc/x!(z|ambient.d).ts") using node --input-type=module -e and bun --eval, then run node --test test/duplication-glob.test.ts and bun test test/duplication-glob.test.ts.
Native Bun and Node accept the same configured negative-extglob scope, or the runtime refuses unsupported scope explicitly before scanning.
Node matches the source and all six contracts pass; Bun returns false and five of six contracts pass. Default packed npm and native Bun duplication gates both pass.
